claims.text: The starting material is an as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a fine lamellar structure.
Annealing at 600–700°C for approximately 24 hours with controlled cooling will induce nanoscale B2-ordered precipitates in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The annealing-induced B2 precipitates will be coherent and uniformly distributed.
The B2 precipitates will be localized along lamellar interfaces.
The nanoscale B2 precipitates will refine the alloy's microstructure.
The B2 precipitates will impede dislocation motion.
The B2 precipitates will impede grain-boundary sliding.
Impeded dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will increase yield strength.
Impeded dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will improve ductility.
The precipitates will inhibit room-temperature creep by anchoring the lamellar structure during sustained loading.
The precipitates will disrupt continuous diffusion paths that facilitate corrosion.
Optimized annealing will improve both yield strength and ductility relative to the as-cast alloy.
Optimized annealing will significantly reduce room-temperature creep under sustained loads relative to the as-cast alloy.
Optimized annealing will improve corrosion resistance under thermal cycling relative to the as-cast alloy.
The combined improvements will allow the alloy to meet more stringent industrial and aerospace-fastener requirements.
The intervention is effective only within a processing window that preserves the fine lamellar structure.
Excessive annealing temperature or duration can coarsen the precipitates.
Precipitate coarsening can compromise ductility and overall performance.
